$description: Layout geometry. Theme-invariant: these do not change between themes or modes. Reading geometry is house style — the measure in particular is an inclusive-design decision, not a preference, and it is the reason this set ships with the package rather than being left to each application. Application chrome dimensions are defaults; a consumer overrides them on :root without touching anything else.

page-w.$description: Maximum page width, including any rails.

content-w.$description: The content column. Wider than the editor's own 680px so tables, code blocks, and diagrams can use the full width while prose stays capped by --measure.

measure.$description: Prose line-length cap, 72 characters. The column itself stays at --content-w; only running prose is constrained. Long lines cost re-reading effort for every reader and disproportionately for dyslexic readers, so this is a hard constraint rather than a stylistic one. Corrected from 68ch in August 2026: the published design system and the accessibility rationale both specified 72, and the implementation was the outlier.

gutter.$description: Horizontal breathing room between the content column and the viewport edge at narrow widths. Equal to --sp-6.

sidebar-w.$description: Navigation rail width. A default: an application with a different rail overrides this.

topbar-h.$description: Fixed top bar height. A default, and the value most applications will want to set --table-sticky-offset to.

table-sticky-offset.$description: How far below the viewport top a sticky table header parks. Defaults to no offset, because the package cannot know whether a consumer has fixed chrome. An application with a top bar sets this to its own height.
